My dear Miss Yonge	
[I ](../persons.html#939)ought to have acknowledged the [copy](../books.html#62) for the new [number ](../others.html#78)earlier, but I wanted to write you a longer letter which I cant do today after all.
I would be glad to see what more you have written of [Bethlehem](../others.html#177), when you have satisfied yourself - or at least approximately - who could satisfy themselves on such a subject.

The young [Artist](../persons.html#500) is ready to [work](../others.html#167) whenever you like.

Shall I [pay](../others.html#160) the monthly sums to your [banker](../others.html#169) in London, or send you a cheque? I have also the £200 for the [Clever Woman](../books.html#58) to pay.

It is indeed glorious weather.

You should see us now at Tooting.

Yours most truly
A.

Macmillan
